en: The Apadāna of the Elder Ekapuṇḍarīka Suvaṇṇabibbohana Chapter 9 I offered a single white lotus to the Buddha, the Great Sage, the Teacher who was like a golden mountain. Because of that deed, I have been reborn in heaven for a hundred thousand aeons. Having passed through many hundreds of thousands of births, I was born as a human being. I am now an elder named Ekapuṇḍarīka; I have attained the state of an Arhat. My body is adorned with the thirty-two marks of a Great Man, and my radiance is like that of the sun and moon. I am a great sage, free from all defilements, and I dwell in the bliss of Nibbāna. This is the fruit of offering a single white lotus to the Buddha. May all beings attain such a state. May they be endowed with wisdom and reach the state of an Arhat. May all beings be happy. May all beings be well. May all beings be free from suffering. May all beings attain the bliss of Nibbāna. May all beings be established in the Dhamma. May all beings be free from fear. May all beings be free from enmity. May all beings be free from affliction. May all beings be established in the path of virtue. May all beings be established in the practice of generosity.

at that time he offered a white lotus ninety-four aeons ago.
I do not know a state of woe;
this is the fruit of the white lotus.
the Buddha’s teaching has been accomplished.
Thus indeed did the Venerable Elder Ekapuṇḍarīka speak these verses.
The legend of the Elder Ekapuṇḍarīka, the ninth.
